Scene 1The Email
Before any visit, Alex needs to find the right person and get a meeting on the calendar. Who should Alex email first?
AMichael Turner, the Maintenance Manager.
BRichard Hall, the VP of Operations.
ToMichael Turner · m.turner@northwind.com
FromAlex Morgan · Ventix Compressors
Quick question about your compressor maintenance

Hi Michael,

My name is Alex Morgan, I work with Ventix Compressors. I noticed Northwind Manufacturing runs equipment similar to what we support at several plants nearby.

Most maintenance teams we talk to are dealing with the same tradeoff: fix it when it breaks, or pay for a plan that prevents the bigger problems. I'd love to learn more about your current approach, no pitch, just a conversation.

Would you have 20 minutes this week for a quick call? Happy to work around your schedule.

Best,
Alex Morgan
Ventix Compressors

Two days later, no response. Alex sends a quick WhatsApp voice message.
0:12
Transcript

"Hey Michael, it's Alex again, from Ventix. Just following up on the email I sent, no pressure at all, I know things get buried in the inbox. If it's easier, I'm happy to just hop on a quick call whenever works for you. Thanks!"

Scene Context

Before Alex can visit anyone, he needs to find the right first contact and get a meeting on the calendar. Most maintenance sales start with an email, not a knock on the door.

Scene Objectives
  • Pick the most useful first contact
  • Keep the email short and specific
  • Give a clear reason to meet
  • Make it easy to say yes
Useful Language
  • I'm reaching out because...Estou entrando em contato porque...
  • Would you have 20 minutes this week for a quick call?Você teria 20 minutos essa semana para uma ligação rápida?
  • I'd love to learn more about your current approach.Adoraria saber mais sobre a abordagem atual de vocês.
  • Happy to work around your schedule.Fico à vontade para me adaptar à sua agenda.
Your Turn to Speak
Pick whichever question fits best
  • Do you think it's better to start with the person who'll actually use the product, or the person who'll approve the budget?
  • Do you think a cold email should ask for a meeting directly, or offer useful information first?
  • Is it better to email the whole team at once, or reach one person at a time?

I think it's better to... because... Eu acho melhor... porque...
In my opinion, ... because... Na minha opinião, ... porque...

Scene 2The Gatekeeper
Alex Morgan
Sales Engineer
×
Linda Carter
Executive Assistant
Good morning! My name is Alex Morgan. I have a 10 a.m. appointment with the Maintenance Manager.
Good morning, Alex. Let me check... May I have your company name, please?
Sure. I'm from Ventix Compressors. We provide industrial maintenance services.
Hmm, I'm not finding anything for a 10 a.m. under that name. Are you sure it was today?
How does Alex respond to the mix-up?
AInsist it must be there and ask her to look again.
BStay calm and offer to show the confirmation email.
Ah, here it is, it was booked under "Facilities", not under your name. Sorry about that. Someone from the maintenance team will be right with you.
What should Alex do next?
AAsk if there's someone else he can speak with.
BWait at the reception.
Scene Context

This is Alex's first visit to Northwind Manufacturing. He needs to get access to the right people and start building relationships.

Scene Objectives
  • Be polite and professional
  • Provide information clearly
  • Start building rapport
  • Get the next step
Useful Language

Scene 3The End User
Alex Morgan
Sales Engineer
×
Carlos Mendes
Maintenance Technician
Hi Carlos, I know you're busy. Just a couple of quick questions, if that's okay?
Sure, go ahead. What do you need?
What's it like working with this compressor day to day? Anything that surprises you?
Honestly, the vibration checks take forever. If that was faster, that'd help a lot.
How does Alex keep him talking, without sounding like he's just checking a box?
AJump straight to explaining how the new model fixes that.
BAsk if it's just the time, or if something else about it bothers him too.
Is it just the time, or does something else about it bother you too?
Both, honestly. Half the time the readings are fine anyway. It's writing everything down by hand that really kills me, not the checking itself.
That's good to know. Would something automated make a real difference?
Definitely. If I could scan a reading instead of logging it by hand, I'd save maybe twenty minutes every visit.
What should Alex do next?
APromise Carlos the new system will fix the logging problem.
BNote down the manual logging detail and mention it later to Michael and Emma.
Scene Context

Michael introduces Alex to Carlos, the technician who actually works on the compressors every day. Carlos is busy and slightly wary of the interruption. The real information is usually one question past the first complaint.

Scene Objectives
  • Show respect for his time
  • Ask a follow-up instead of jumping to a solution
  • Find the specific, concrete detail behind the complaint
  • Build trust with the person who'll notice if something goes wrong
Useful Language
  • I won't take much of your time.Não vou tomar muito do seu tempo.
  • What's it like working with this day to day?Como é trabalhar com isso no dia a dia?
  • Is it just the time, or something else too?É só o tempo, ou tem mais alguma coisa também?
  • Would something automated make a difference?Algo automatizado faria diferença?
Your Turn to Speak
Pick whichever question fits best
  • Do you think a salesperson should always ask a follow-up question, even when a complaint sounds small?
  • Is it better to ask an end user open questions, or specific yes/no questions?
  • Should a salesperson take notes during a casual conversation, or does that make people less open?

Scene 4The Technical Buyer
Alex Morgan
Sales Engineer
×
Michael Turner
Maintenance Manager
We've had two unplanned stops this year already. What makes your maintenance plan different?
Based on the running hours we're seeing, most failures like these are preventable with scheduled vibration checks and filter replacement.
That's what the last vendor said too.
Michael goes quiet and crosses his arms. How does Alex read the silence?
AFill the silence with more reasons the plan will work.
BLet the silence sit, and wait for him to respond.
Alright. Send me the data. But I want the failure modes too, not just an uptime number.
Understood. I'll include the root cause data, not just the summary.
What should Alex do next?
AOffer to share real performance data, including failure modes.
BInsist that this plan is definitely better, without proof.
Scene Context

Michael has reviewed the compressor's maintenance history. He's skeptical of vendors who oversell and underdeliver.

Scene Objectives
  • Show real technical knowledge
  • Answer with data, not just promises
  • Acknowledge limits honestly
  • Earn credibility, not just agreement
Useful Language
  • Based on the running hours, I'd recommend...Com base nas horas de operação, eu recomendaria...
  • I want the failure modes, not just an uptime number.Eu quero os tipos de falha, não só um número de disponibilidade.
  • I'll include the root cause data, not just a summary.Vou incluir os dados de causa raiz, não só um resumo.
  • Would it help to see data from a similar client?Ajudaria ver dados de um cliente parecido?
Your Turn to Speak
Pick whichever question fits best
  • Do you think a salesperson should answer a skeptical question with data, or with a story?
  • Do you think silence in a conversation is something to fill, or something to respect?
  • Is it better to admit a competitor did something well, or avoid mentioning them at all?

Scene 5The Champion
Alex Morgan
Sales Engineer
×
Emma Brooks
Reliability Engineer
I think this could really help, but I'll need to explain it to people who don't care about vibration data.
What would help you make the case internally?
Something simple. Like, what does this actually prevent, in plain terms?
I'll put that in writing so you have it in hand, plain language, no jargon.
How should Alex frame what he sends her?
AAs a copy of the official sales proposal, so it looks professional.
BAs talking points she can put in her own words.
Is there someone specific you're worried about convincing?
Michael, honestly. He'll want to know this isn't just marketing dressed up as data.
Good to know. I'll make sure the numbers are front and center, not buried in the middle.
What should Alex send her?
AThe full technical proposal, so Michael sees everything.
BA short, non-technical summary she can forward as her own.
Scene Context

Emma believes in improving reliability, but she needs a way to justify this internally without looking like she's just following a vendor's pitch.

Scene Objectives
  • Give her language she can reuse internally
  • Make her look good for suggesting this
  • Ask what resistance she expects
  • Turn her into an advocate, not just a contact
Useful Language
  • What would help you make the case internally?O que ajudaria você a defender isso internamente?
  • Something you could put in your own words...Algo que você possa colocar com suas próprias palavras...
  • I don't want to put you in an awkward position.Não quero te colocar numa posição desconfortável.
  • What would carry weight with Michael?O que teria peso pro Michael?
Your Turn to Speak

Scene 6The Economic Buyer
Alex Morgan
Sales Engineer
×
Sarah Mitchell
Plant Director
I have fifteen minutes. What's the bottom line?
In the interest of time: this plan costs less than one unplanned breakdown, and prevents multiple ones a year.
And if I say yes today?
Sarah glances at her watch. How does Alex use the little time he has left?
AStart explaining the technical details of the plan.
BAsk if she has any concerns before committing.
Just one. My last vendor promised no delays too, and then took three weeks to show up.
Fair concern. We schedule the first inspection this month, and I'll put that date in writing, so it's not just a promise.
What should Alex do next?
AAsk directly if she's ready to move forward.
BWait for her to bring up next steps herself.
Scene Context

Sarah has fifteen minutes. She doesn't want a sales pitch, she wants numbers.

Scene Objectives
  • Lead with cost comparison, not features
  • Speak to ROI directly
  • Respect her time
  • Ask for the decision, don't just hope for it
Useful Language
  • In the interest of time, here's the bottom line...Pra economizar tempo, o resumo é o seguinte...
  • Do you have any concerns before we move forward?Você tem alguma preocupação antes de avançarmos?
  • I'll put that in writing, so it's not just a promise.Vou colocar isso por escrito, pra não ser só uma promessa.
  • Can we agree on next steps today?Podemos alinhar os próximos passos hoje?
Your Turn to Speak
Pick whichever question fits best
  • Do you think it's better to lead with a number, or with a short story, when you only have a few minutes with a decision maker?
  • Should a salesperson ask about concerns before pitching, or after?
  • Is it better to promise an exact date, or a general timeframe?

Scene 7The Blocker
Alex Morgan
Sales Engineer
×
Frank Dawson
Production Supervisor
Nobody asked me about this. We've always fixed things when they break. Why change now?
That's a fair question. You've been running this line longer than anyone, what's your biggest concern?
Extra cost for something that might not even happen.
Frank crosses his arms and looks away. How does Alex respond in the moment?
APush back right away with a counter-argument.
BPause and let the silence sit for a moment.
Look, last time someone "upgraded" something here, it caused more downtime than it saved. I don't want that on my line again.
That makes sense, that's a real reason to be careful. Was that a different vendor, or a different kind of change?
Different vendor. But I don't have a great track record trusting "the new thing" either way.
I hear that. Can I follow up with the actual numbers, so it's not just my word?
What should Alex do next?
AExplain why this vendor and this situation are different.
BAcknowledge his experience and offer to follow up with data.
Scene Context

Frank wasn't part of the earlier conversations. He's hearing about this for the first time, and he's already skeptical.

Scene Objectives
  • Don't get defensive
  • Acknowledge his experience
  • Find out what specifically worries him
  • Avoid trying to win the argument on the spot
Useful Language
  • That makes sense, that's a real reason to be careful.Faz sentido, é um motivo real pra ter cautela.
  • I'm not asking you to trust me yet.Não estou pedindo pra você confiar em mim ainda.
  • That's a fair point, can I follow up on that?É um ponto justo, posso retomar isso depois?
  • I'm not here to change everything overnight.Não estou aqui pra mudar tudo da noite pro dia.
Your Turn to Speak
Pick whichever question fits best
  • Do you think resistance to change is usually about the change itself, or about something else, like trust or a past bad experience?
  • Should a salesperson try to win an argument with a skeptic, or let it go unresolved for now?
  • Is it better to ask a skeptic direct questions, or give them space to talk without interruption?

Scene 8The Group Presentation
Alex is about to present the maintenance agreement in a meeting room. Before you see who's actually there, guess: who do you think will be in the room? Click on everyone you'd expect.
Michael, Emma, Sarah, and David, exactly the four people most likely to sit in on a technical and budget presentation like this one.
What Alex Is Actually Proposing
The plan, side by side with how things work today at Northwind.
TodayReactive maintenance. You fix it after it breaks.
→
ProposedScheduled vibration checks and filter replacement.
TodayTwo unplanned stops this year already.
→
ProposedMost of those failures are preventable in advance.
TodayAn unplanned breakdown, which always costs more, and never happens at a convenient time.
→
ProposedA fixed, predictable cost, in writing.
TodayEmergency stop misuse causes premature wear, and can void the warranty.
→
ProposedProper training on what the equipment is, and isn't, built for.
TodayA past vendor promised no delays, then took three weeks to show up.
→
ProposedFirst inspection scheduled this month, no delay.
Scene Context

Not every stakeholder attends every meeting. A first presentation usually draws the people who need to evaluate and champion it, not yet the final approvers. There's always a tradeoff between speed and getting everyone in the room.

Scene Objectives
  • Predict who has a reason to be there
  • Understand why some stakeholders are missing
  • Notice that the room changes as the deal moves forward
Useful Language
  • Thanks everyone for making time today.Obrigado a todos por reservarem um tempo hoje.
  • I'll keep this focused, since I know your time is limited.Vou manter isso direto, já que sei que o tempo de vocês é limitado.
  • Happy to go deeper on that after the meeting.Fico à vontade pra aprofundar isso depois da reunião.
  • Let's align on next steps before we close.Vamos alinhar os próximos passos antes de encerrar.

Pick whichever question fits best

  • Should a presenter mention people who aren't in the room, or focus only on those who are?
  • Is it better to ask for a decision at the end of a meeting, or let people think it over?
